title: Principal neighbourhood of an algebraic field spectrum image in an affine scheme
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $k$ a field [def-weil-field], and $A$ a commutative $k$-algebra such that every element of $A$ satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in $k$. No domain, reducedness, finite-dimensionality, or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed on $A$. Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be any ring homomorphism, and let $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi):\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every open subset $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $h(|\operatorname{Spec}A|)$, there exists $f\in R$ such that $h(|\operatorname{Spec}A|)\subseteq D(f)\subseteq W$, where $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$.

source.place: Tag 0E21, lemma-ample-profinite-set-in-principal-affine, affine case X = Spec R and L = O_X; D(f) is X_s after the canonical trivialization of O_X tensor powers.

proof.text: Let G consist of all g in R such that D_R(g) is contained in W. The basic-open basis [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] and the image hypothesis show that the D_A(phi(g)) for g in G cover Spec A. By the unit-ideal criterion [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], 1 belongs to the ideal generated by these images. Express ideal membership by a finitely supported linear combination, obtaining finitely many g_i with D_R(g_i) contained in W and coefficients a_i in A satisfying sum_i a_i phi(g_i)=1. This works also for the zero ring and an empty support.

source.place: Tag 0E21, lemma-ample-profinite-set-in-principal-affine, affine specialization; quasi-compactness reduction and finite-stage preparation

proof.text: Let B be the k-subalgebra of A generated by the finitely many a_i and phi(g_i). Every generator is integral by hypothesis, so [lem-sc-finite-generated-integral-subring] makes B finite over k. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian], B is Artinian; [lem-sfb-artinian-spectrum-finite] gives a finite prime spectrum, including when B is the zero ring. Lift the unit relation to B using the injectivity of its inclusion into A.

source.place: Tag 0E21, lemma-ample-profinite-set-in-principal-affine, affine specialization; finite k-subalgebra reduction and finiteness of its spectrum

proof.text: Let S be the inverse-image subring phi^{-1}(B) of R and psi:S -> B the restriction of phi. Each g_i lies in S. Let J be the ideal of S generated by the g_i. For every prime q of B, its contraction P_q along psi is prime. If J were contained in P_q, every psi(g_i) would lie in q, so the unit relation would put 1 in q, a contradiction.

source.place: Tag 0E21, lemma-ample-profinite-set-in-principal-affine, affine specialization; explicit affine finite-type integer stage, retaining the finite field-algebra factorization

proof.text: The family P_q is finite by Step 2. If Spec B is empty, take f=0 in J. Otherwise apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] to J and all the P_q, using the noncontainments from Step 3, to obtain f in J outside every P_q. Thus in either case psi(f) lies in no prime ideal of B.

source.place: Tag 0E21, lemma-ample-profinite-set-in-principal-affine, affine specialization; finite-set principal-neighbourhood step, using prime avoidance as in the affine case of Properties lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine

proof.text: View f as an element of R. Every prime Q of A contracts under the inclusion B -> A to a prime q of B. Avoidance of P_q therefore says phi(f) is not in Q, proving that the whole image of Spec A lies in D_R(f). Conversely, a prime p of R outside W contains every g_i, since D_R(g_i) is contained in W. Its contraction to S contains J by the universal property of ideal span, hence contains f. Taking the contrapositive proves D_R(f) is contained in W.

source.place: Tag 0E21, lemma-ample-profinite-set-in-principal-affine, affine specialization; pull back the finite-stage principal function and verify both inclusions explicitly

proof_origin.place: Tag 0E21, affine specialization of the finite-stage and finite-set argument; C7 Lean implementation uses the inverse-image subring phi^{-1}(B) instead of the smaller integer-generated subring, and proves the final inclusions directly by contraction and ideal span.
